edges.rationale: SNR is the ratio of received signal power to noise; understanding how attenuation and path loss reduce received power with distance is needed to explain why SNR falls and BER rises as sender-receiver distance grows.

Interference from other sources in the same band and multipath fading constitute the noise and channel-variation side of SNR; without these concepts the relationship between SNR, changing channel conditions, and bit errors cannot be explained.

edges.dependent: Wireless Link Rates and Coverage Ranges
edges.rationale: Coverage distances of wireless standards are fundamentally limited by path loss, and transmission rates dropping with distance are a direct consequence of attenuation; path loss is needed to explain how rates and coverage vary with distance.

edges.dependent: Wireless Link Rates and Coverage Ranges
edges.rationale: Achievable transmission rates under varying channel conditions are determined by the SNR/BER relationship; comparing standards' rates and how they degrade with distance and conditions presupposes understanding SNR and BER.

CDMA is a solution to the problem of multiple users transmitting simultaneously over the same spectrum; appreciating why simultaneous transmissions interfere motivates the use of unique code sequences to separate users.
